The fluorescent lights of the office hummed with the same low-grade anxiety that had been building in Arthur’s chest since he clipped the cage to his desk. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Arthur had made a critical error in judgment: he had brought Barnaby, his African Grey parrot, who didn’t just mimic sounds, but had developed a disturbing habit of eavesdropping on Arthur’s late-night strategy calls with the CEO.

Arthur had spent the morning frantically trying to teach Barnaby to say "Good morning" and "Nice weather." Instead, as the VP of Marketing, Linda, walked by to drop off a quarterly report, Barnaby puffed his feathers and squawked, "The Q3 projections are fabricated! We’re bleeding cash!"

The room went silent. Linda froze, her coffee cup halfway to her lips. Arthur’s face drained of color. He lunged for the cage, whispering, "No, no, Barnaby, that’s a metaphor! A poetic metaphor about liquidity!"

Linda narrowed her eyes. "A metaphor for embezzlement?"

"No! Just... avian existential dread!" Arthur stammered, trying to cover the cage with a handkerchief. But Barnaby, sensing the tension, decided to escalate. He leaned out of the mesh and croaked, "The merger is a sham! The CEO is actually a penguin!"

Linda dropped her coffee. It splashed across the carpet, but nobody moved to clean it up. They were too busy watching Arthur try to stuff a stress ball into the parrot’s beak.

"I need to get him out of here," Arthur hissed to his colleague, Dave, who was pretending to be very interested in a spreadsheet. "He’s going to leak the proprietary algorithm next."

"Maybe if you just bribe him?" Dave suggested, not looking up.

Arthur grabbed a handful of premium sunflower seeds from his desk drawer and shoved them toward Barnaby. "Eat! Eat the silence!"

Barnaby ignored the seeds. Instead, he picked up a pen, held it like a microphone, and squawked in a perfect impression of the CEO’s voice: "Arthur, you’re fired. Also, I know about the dental floss incident."

Arthur froze. "The what?"
